subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 54-year-old man with a prior myocardial infarction has an LDL cholesterol of 176 mg/dL despite 6 months of dietary therapy. He is started on simvastatin, and 8 weeks later his LDL cholesterol is 98 mg/dL. He remains asymptomatic, and liver transaminases and creatine kinase are normal.
question: Simvastatin lowers LDL cholesterol by inhibiting which of the following enzymes?
explanation_correct: HMG-CoA reductase catalyzes the rate-limiting, committed step of cholesterol synthesis, the reduction of HMG-CoA to mevalonate by the enzyme anchored in the endoplasmic reticulum membrane. Statins are competitive inhibitors of this enzyme, so hepatic cholesterol synthesis falls and intracellular sterol levels drop.

explanation_incorrect.A: HMG-CoA synthase generates HMG-CoA upstream of the reductase and is the rate-limiting enzyme of ketogenesis, not the target of statins.
explanation_incorrect.B: HMG-CoA lyase catalyzes the final step of ketone body production in mitochondria and is not inhibited by statins.
explanation_incorrect.D: Squalene monooxygenase acts several steps downstream of mevalonate and is not the pharmacologic target of statins.
explanation_incorrect.E: ACAT esterifies cholesterol for storage in cells and is not the site of action of statins.

educationalObjective: Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme of cholesterol synthesis.
